author: host parallel CLI execution worker
explanation: The direct program is strict and demo-consistent, working in visible coordinates. It reads from pixels: frame = corner colour; full frame-coloured lines on one axis = panel dividers; panel background = unique most common interior colour. It checks that each panel motif is a pure translation of the previous one with a constant step. Output = one framed panel with the last motif moved one more step. Its hypotheses are the time direction ORDER in {+1,-1}. Each one is checked against EVERY demo by full-grid equality. All survivors must agree on the full query output, otherwise it raises Inconsistent/Ambiguous: no default, majority vote, demo skipping or reset. d4/palette are unused (no hidden D4 choice).

fixture_conflict.summary: Canonical train pair 2 (validate() uses extra=1) labels the 2x2 frame-coloured motif at rows 12-13. The native rule gives rows 11-12. That input can be generated EXACTLY by the native fresh sampler (random.seed(15323); generate()) with the rows 11-12 label. This identical-input / different-output conflict means no function of the input can match both. The audit also scores each train pair as a query with all demos, pair 2 included. So every demo-consistent uniform program fails all 16 canonical variants. The previous draft passed only by learning a +1 residual from pair 2 itself (a self-referential lookup with default 0).

witness.explicit: generate(width=4,frames=3,offset=3,flip=0,colors=[8,2,8],pattern=[1,1,1,1]) input == canonical train[1] input, output differs

fixture_conflict.feature_keyed_rules_refuted: Pair 2 alone carries "+1" features: motif colour == frame colour, solid 2x2 motif, or conjunctions such as frames==3 & flip==0. Fresh draws produce all of them with residual 0, so any keyed +1 rule contradicts constructor labels. The canonical demos also cannot choose among keyed rules (e.g. "step>=2 and moving down" also separates pair 2 from pairs 1 and 3, and it predicts +1 on the canonical test). So the residual is not identifiable from context.
fixture_conflict.intrinsic_vs_context: In the native family (extra=0), every one of 8000 fresh pair-checks (1000 pairs x 8 D4, shuffled palette) is identifiable from its input alone: independent enumeration gives one output, equal to the label. Each single demo identifies ORDER (0 evidence-missing cases, 0 demo resamples needed). If extra in {0,1} is admitted as a latent parameter, all 250/250 base queries become intrinsically ambiguous. The fixture defect is therefore intrinsic, not a context shortfall.
